security_problem: A valid tools/call can reach the downstream stdio or remote transport even when its final allow event was never durably appended to the hash-linked JSONL audit ledger: Logger.Log swallows write/short-write errors and advances chain state before the write is known to have succeeded, and all three terminal allow branches forward unconditionally after best-effort logging. Additionally, chain state was recovered from a separate pre-open path read while appends go through a different fd, so a rotated/rebound configured audit path can either carry a stale recovered chain onto a fresh inode or authorize a commit written through a stale fd whose inode no longer matches the configured path.
required_behavior: For every valid tools/call C, downstream_transport_received(C) implies a full, hash-linked EventToolAllowed record for C completed on the configured regular O_SYNC JSONL ledger before the downstream write began. Logger.CommitAuthorization accepts only terminal allow events, requires a regular durable sink, performs a full-write check, poisons the logger on write/short-write failure, and advances hash-chain state only after success. NewLogger recovers or initializes the hash chain from the exact O_SYNC append fd: a fresh exclusive-create always starts at genesis; an existing inode is recovered through the fd that will receive appends; every authorization commit validates live fd regularity and fd-to-configured-path device+inode identity immediately before and immediately after its write, failing closed (ErrAuditSinkChanged/ErrNonDurableSink) on any rotation, rename, unlink, replacement, symlink-to-different-inode, or non-regular rebinding, poisoning the logger, and leaving in-memory chain state unchanged. Approved, explicit, and default/fallback allow branches commit before returning "forward"; any commit failure produces a generic client deny and zero stdio/remote relay. Metrics and session taints mutate only after commit success. Omitted/invalid AuditLogPath fails closed.
failure_behavior: Fail closed: sink failure, short write, closed logger, non-durable sink, poisoned logger, or a rotated/rebound configured audit path (missing, renamed, unlinked, replaced, atomic-renamed-over, symlinked to a different inode, or non-regular) denies the valid tools/call with no relay on either transport, no allow/approved metric, no session taint, and no in-memory chain advance.
